description.narrative:
Uganda’s seed sector is comprised of the formal and informal seed systems, these systems are both recognized in the National Seed Policy (2018) and provides strategic direction for development of both sectors. The informal seed sector contributes over 85% of the seed supply, however its affected by several challenges leading to low poor quality seeds and ultimately agricultural productivity. Despite the critical role of the informal sector and its inclusion in the policy, it remains not well understood by the key stakeholders and the specific legal and regulatory support needed to enhance its effectiveness. Several approaches have been promoted by various actors to improve performance of farmer managed seed systems (referred to as informal systems), these include; community seed banking, participatory plant breeding, farmer seed enterprise development among others. These are however not well understood by the critical sector players and policy makers which negatively affects the legal and regulatory support given to the sub sector. For example, much as the National Seed policy provides for farmers to engage in seed production and marketing, it restrict them to specificcrops that are not of interest to the private sector and the source of parent seed must also be from a “known sources” such as national agricultural research organization and private seed breeders and companies. This is made worse by the fact that majoring of seed varieties managed by farmers are not even registered in the National seed catalogue. There is also a very strong involvement of Uganda Seed Traders Association (an association of seed companies with the primary aim of fostering their business interest) in the issuance of Quality Declared Seed certificates, including printing anddistribution of the certificates.
ESAFF Uganda’s role will include capturing farmers voices and messages for publicity, organizing a policy review workshop on National Seed Act and the National Seed Policy to develop position paper(s), supporting the review of the position paper by the “Think Tank” . They will also coordinate with PELUM to supporting analysis of safety and security of farmers and seeking legal advice before publicizing farmers voices collected by ESAFF

participating-org.narrative:
In 2002, Participatory Ecological Land Use Management (PELUM) Association, a regional network, conceived an exciting idea of a Small Farmers Convergence (SFC) alongside the World Summit on Sustainable Agriculture in Johannesburg. The main aim of the convergence was to make small farmers, pastoralists and fisher folk, who are central to sustainable natural resource management and development,more visible The Small Farmers Convergence was rated a success in terms of increased visibility of farmers, representation on the CSO International Steering Group, exposure and capacity building of the farmers but most important was the identity and solidarity that developed amongst the farmers. The 300 delegates of the Small Farmer Convergence, decided to set up a Regional Forum of Small-scale farmers, pastoralists and traditional fisher folks which was called the East and Southern African Farmers Forum (ESAFF). The rationale for the Regional Forum was to consolidate the development of a farmer movement and build on common aspirations, learning andlinkages made during the SFC.
Formation stage-after the inception of ESAFF Uganda, leadership was elected and then farmers were mobilised in the 14 districts. Every district then elected a committee that was to runthe activities of ESAFF at the grass root level.ESAFF Uganda then developed its constitution, articles of association and Memorandum of association which documents were later usedto register it. The constitution does not discriminate against women or men or youth, leadership is open to all as long as one has the ability to lead. The ESAFF national board is comprised mainly of women with the ratio of men: women being 2:5. The institution right now is in the process of strengthening its membership at the grassroots and the secretariat too. ESAFGF Uganda has not receivedfunding from Oxfam Novib before. However, Oxfam Great Britain has funded a pilot (1.1.08-31.12.08) to increase participation of ssfin budgeting processes.
